title: Nasi Goreng
subtitle: Indonesian fried rice with prawns and egg
excerpt: Nasi goreng is the Indonesian term for fried rice, and it is one of the most widely eaten dishes in the country. Day-old rice is essential: freshly cooked rice is too moist and will steam in the wok rather than fry. Dark soy sauce gives the dish its distinctive deep colour.
sourceNotes: Nasi goreng has been eaten across Indonesia and the wider Malay archipelago for centuries, born of a practical need to use leftover rice. It is considered one of the national dishes of Indonesia and appears on everything from street stalls to hotel breakfast menus.

content.text: The wok must be  hot before anything goes in. If you are cooking on a domestic hob, let the wok smoke for a full minute before adding the oil.

items.prepNote: day-old cooked rice, cold and broken up

content.text: Heat the wok over the highest heat until it begins to smoke. Add the sunflower oil, then the garlic, onion, and chilli. Stir-fry for 1 minute.
Add the prawns and toss for 2 minutes until they turn pink. Push everything to the side of the wok.
Add the shredded cabbage to the centre of the wok and stir-fry for 1 minute. Then add the cold rice, breaking up any clumps with the spatula.
Pour the dark soy sauce around the edge of the wok and add the palm sugar. Toss everything together vigorously for 2 to 3 minutes until the rice is coated and beginning to char in places.
Push the rice to the sides. Crack the eggs into the centre and scramble lightly, then fold into the rice before the eggs fully set. Scatter the spring onion over the top and serve immediately.

items.cause: The rice was too moist, or the wok was not hot enough
items.fix: Spread the rice in a thin layer and leave it without stirring for 30 seconds before tossing. This allows a light crust to form.

items.cause: Not enough soy sauce, or the wok lost heat when ingredients were added
items.fix: Add another splash of dark soy sauce and a pinch of salt. Make sure the wok is back up to full heat before adding each ingredient.
